name: Tape Echo
purpose: Roland Space Echo style tape delay with three playback heads and a spring reverb: warm, dark, slightly wobbly echoes that get softer and smudgier with each repeat; classic for vocal throws, dub, rockabilly slapback and psychedelic guitar.
avoid_for: anything that must stay clean and precise

params.name: Head select
params.ai_hint: Active heads/spring. Head 1 short slapback, 2 medium, 3 long; combos add multi-tap repeats. '+ Reverb' choices add the spring (set reverb_level). 'Reverb only' = spring with no echo.

params.name: Repeat rate
params.ai_hint: Tape speed: 0 = slow and long, 100 = fast and short. Head 1: 177 to 69 ms, Head 2: 337 to 131 ms, Head 3: 489 to 189 ms. Slapback is 60-80 on Head 1.

params.name: Intensity
params.ai_hint: Feedback. 0-15 one or two repeats, 25-40 a few, 50-65 long trails. Above ~75 it self-oscillates and runs away: stay under 65 unless a drone is wanted.

params.name: Echo volume
params.ai_hint: Level of the echo return before the Mix control. 30-60 is typical.

params.name: Reverb volume
params.ai_hint: Spring reverb level; heard only in the '+ Reverb' and 'Reverb only' selections. 20-40 splashy spring, more for dub.

params.name: Bass
params.ai_hint: Shapes the echoes only. Cut (-30 to -60) so repeats do not muddy a vocal; 0 is neutral.

params.name: Treble
params.ai_hint: Shapes the echoes only. Negative values darken the repeats and tuck them behind the source; positive adds bite.

params.name: Input volume
params.ai_hint: Drives the tape input stage. 50 is normal; higher saturates and thickens the echoes, lower is cleaner.

params.name: Wow and flutter
params.ai_hint: Tape speed wobble. 0 = the machine's natural subtle movement; 20-50 obvious vintage drift; more is woozy.

params.name: Tape age
params.ai_hint: New = clean and bright with very little noise. Used = a little loss and noise. Old = dull, noisy, wobbly, with a tape splice that can be heard.

params.name: Mix
params.ai_hint: Dry/wet crossfade: 0 dry only, 50 keeps dry and echo/spring both at full level, 100 wet only. Use 50 as an insert and lower Echo volume for quieter echoes.

notes: Parameters are written by hand against the framework-free TapeEchoDSP core (Tape Echo 2 by Dusk Audio, GPL-3.0-or-later). Host tempo sync, pans, output trim, noise level, hum frequency and the record-input switch are not exposed and stay at the upstream defaults.
Tape Echo 2 is pinned to a newer Dusk Audio commit than the other Dusk modules (source key dusk-audio-echo).
Self-oscillation (Intensity above about 75%) is intentional upstream and can exceed 0 dBFS.
There is no host tempo input: work out the time by ear, or use Clean Delay when exact note values are needed.
The stereo input is summed inside the tape and spring paths.
CPU: 3.5% of one core at 48 kHz on Plugsalot's 2-core build machine (plugin/tests/TestMain.cpp); 1 point per 2%.
